candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: L33718 is the PAP device policy that directly covers E0601 CPAP for treatment of obstructive sleep apnea. Its initial coverage criteria (in-person clinical evaluation before the sleep test, and a qualifying sleep test) match this patient: an in-person evaluation on 2026-08-18 preceded the 2026-08-30 polysomnography, which showed AHI 14 with 91 events over 6.5 hours and an SpO2 nadir of 83%, and the order was placed 2026-09-05. L36902 is a sleep-testing policy that defines the OSA diagnostic threshold but does not govern the device, and L33405 addresses APAP/BPAP without covering CPAP for this patient's condition.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: Dr. Whitney250 Wiza601 saw the patient in person on 2026-08-18 to evaluate possible obstructive sleep apnea (R95; encounter R37). The sleep study was performed on 2026-08-30 (R38), so the evaluation came before the sleep test.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. AHI or RDI greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or 2. AHI or RDI greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of a. excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or b. hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: The AHI is 14 events per hour with 91 total events over 6.5 hours (R56, R85, R88, R90), so alternative 1 (AHI of 15 or more) is not met. Alternative 2 applies because the AHI is 14 with at least 10 events, but the record does not document the required condition. The patient denies daytime sleepiness and his Epworth score is 8, which is in the normal range (R95, R69). No mood disorder or insomnia is documented; the GAD-7 and PHQ-2 scores are low (R72, R78). Blood pressures are 127/77 and 123/80 with no hypertension diagnosis, and there is no documented ischemic heart disease or stroke history (R57, R58). The record contradicts the sleepiness requirement and does not contain any of the listed conditions.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: A DME supplier gave instruction on the use and care of the CPAP device on 2026-09-11 (R55), after the 2026-09-05 order (R32).

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: The sleep study was an attended in-laboratory polysomnography, a Type I facility-based study performed with a sleep center technologist and reported on 2026-09-02 (R38, R90). The record does not document every NCD validity element, but it names the required test type and setting.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test results fail the AHI criteria in effect. The AHI of 14 events per hour is below 15, and the record documents no qualifying symptom or comorbidity for the 5 to 14 range (see I.B).

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: Dr. Whitney250 Wiza601, the treating practitioner, ordered the attended in-laboratory polysomnography, and the 2026-08-18 note documents the order for the sleep study.

decision_explanation: Criterion I.B is not met. The AHI of 14 events per hour does not reach the 15-event threshold, and the record does not document the excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorder, insomnia, hypertension, ischemic heart disease or stroke history that the 5 to 14 range requires. The patient denies daytime sleepiness, his Epworth score is 8, and his blood pressures are normal. Because the sleep test results fail the coverage criteria in effect (Sleep Tests.3), the E0601 claim is denied as not reasonable and necessary.
